nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, exalted be His majesty and hallowed be His names: ﴿الۤر﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "I am Allah; I see (anā Allāhu arā)."
The explanation of these letters has already preceded.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾.
That is, these are those verses, the ones you were promised in the Torah.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِي غَيَابَةِ ٱلْجُبِّ﴾.
Al-ghayāba according to the lexicographers is anything that is hidden from you; and al-jubb is a well that is not lined [with stone].
It is narrated that the jubb here is the well of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). It is from جَبَيْتُ, i.e. I cut, as though it was cut and nothing was done to it after the cutting.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The one who said to them ﴿لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ﴾ is the one who said ﴿فَلَنْ أبْرَحَ الأرْضَ حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أَبِي﴾, and he was the eldest of them.
Someone else said: It was Judah (Yahūdhā), and he was the strongest of them.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَداً نَرْتَعْ وَنَلْعَبْ﴾.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj from Mujāhid, and Warqāʾ from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: That is, we will guard and watch over one another.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ added in his narration: and we will keep watch over one another.
Hārūn said: I asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him: How could they say "وَنَلْعَبُ" (and we will play) when they were prophets? He said: They were not prophets at that time.
And whoever reads "يرتعْ ويلعبْ" with the yāʾ, its meaning in my view is: he will graze the camels; one says رعى and ارتعى with one meaning. This is the reading of the people of Medina.
And it is narrated from Mujāhid ﴿نَرْتِع﴾ with the nūn and kasra on the tāʾ; one says أرتع صاحبَهُ وإبِلَهُ فرتعت, i.e. they stayed in the pasture; and Allah knows best what he intended.
The people of Kufa read ﴿يَرْتَعْ ويَلْعَبْ﴾ with sukūn on the ʿayn, and its meaning is: he will enjoy plenty and eat freely. One says رتعتِ الإِبلُ when the camels graze as they please, and likewise other [animals]; and أرعيتُها: I left them to graze. And one says "فلانٌ راتعٌ", i.e. living in plenty; and from it is:
تَرْتَعُ ما غَفَلَتْ حَتَّى إذَ ادَّكَرتْ * فَإنَّمَا هِيَ إقْبَالٌ وإدْبَارُ
(She grazes freely as long as she forgets, until when she remembers, she is all coming and going.)
And likewise is the meaning of (نَرْتَعْ) with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ʿayn, which is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Mecca.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿نَرْتَعْ﴾: we will be lively and amuse ourselves; and this is like the first meaning.
As for Abū ʿAmr's argument that they were not prophets at that time, there is no need for it, because it is not play that turns one away from the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Why not a virgin, whom you would play with and who would play with you?!"

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَـٰذَا وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
The meaning may be: We revealed to him in the well while they were not aware of that revelation; this is the view of Qatāda.
And the meaning may be: You will surely inform them of this deed of theirs while they do not perceive [who you are].

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿قَالُواْ يَٰأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ﴾.
That is, we were competing in shooting.
And the meaning: we were racing one another in archery.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ﴾.
That is, you have suspected us, and it has settled in your heart that we do not tell the truth, so you will not believe us.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَجَآءُوا عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It was the blood of a young goat.
Sufyān narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "When he looked at it he said: You have lied; had the wolf eaten him, it would have torn the shirt."
Al-Ḥasan said: When he looked at the blood and saw no slit or tear in the shirt, he said: "I have never known the wolf to be so gentle."
And the meaning: with blood possessed of falsehood, i.e. lied about.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْراً﴾.
That is, made it seem attractive.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾.
And it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about beautiful patience and said: "It is that which has no complaint with it."
And the meaning according to the people of reasoning: that which has no complaint with it accompanied by lack of contentment with Allah's decree. So if the complaint is to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He — as He said ﴿إنِّي مَسَّنِي الضُّرُّ﴾ and ﴿إنَّمَا أشْكُو بَثِّي وحُزْنِي إلى اللهِ﴾ — or if it is with contentment, then the one who makes it is patient, as the Prophet ﷺ said in his illness: "Rather I [should say]: O my head!"

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ﴾.
That is, a party of travellers.
﴿فَأَرْسَلُواْ وَارِدَهُمْ﴾: he is the one who goes down [to the water] to draw water.
﴿فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُ﴾.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: One says أدليتُ الدَّلْوَ when you let the bucket down, and دلوتُها when you draw it up.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰبُشْرَىٰ هَـٰذَا غُلاَمٌ﴾.
Al-Suddī and al-Aʿmash said: His name was Bushrā.
Others said: The meaning is: O glad tidings!
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the correct view, because most of the readers read ﴿يٰبُشْرَىٰ هَـٰذَا غُلاَمٌ﴾.
The meaning of calling out to the glad tidings is to alert whoever is present, and it is more emphatic than saying "I rejoiced", just as you say يَا عَجَبَاهُ (O wonder!), i.e. O wonder, this is one of your days — or one of your signs — so be present. This is the doctrine of Sībawayh.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَاعَةً﴾.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿أسرُّوهُ﴾: [that is,] the one who let down the bucket and those with him [kept him secret] from the rest of the merchants, lest they demand a share in him once they knew his price; and they said: "We have only taken him as merchandise [entrusted to us]."
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: They kept his sale secret. On this view the meaning refers to the brothers, as it is narrated that when he was found, his brothers made out that he was merchandise belonging to the people of the water.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾.
The meaning may be: We have sent down the Qurʾān in Arabic.
And the meaning may be: We have sent down the account of Joseph; and this is closer to the meaning, because it is narrated that the Jews said: "Ask him why the family of Jacob moved from Syria to Egypt, and about the account of Joseph." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent this down in Mecca in agreement with what is in the Torah.
And there are additions in it which they did not have. So it is as though this Prophet ﷺ, when he informed them — never having read a book, nor being in a place of books — was in the same rank as Jesus, peace be upon him, bringing the dead to life.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ﴾.
That is, of short value; al-bakhs is deficiency.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Al-bakhs is little, and the "counted" were twenty dirhams.
Qatāda said: ﴿بخسٍ﴾, i.e. wrongful.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿بخسٍ﴾, i.e. unlawful.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and Nawf that they said: They bought him for twenty dirhams.
Mujāhid said: "وشروه", i.e. they sold him when the one who let down the bucket brought him out; they sold him for twenty-two dirhams, and they were eleven.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: He only said "counted" to indicate how few they were, because they would weigh nothing less than an ūqiyya, and the ūqiyya is forty dirhams.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّاهِدِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: One of the exegetes said: They had little desire for him only because of their little knowledge of his standing with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِي ٱشْتَرَاهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لاِمْرَأَتِهِ أَكْرِمِي مَثْوَاهُ﴾.
That is, his stay; and the meaning: honour him during his stay. From it is ثَويتُ في المكان when you reside in a place, as the poet said:
* "رُبَّ ثَاوٍ يُمَلُّ منهُ الثَّوَاءُ" *
(Many a lodger's long stay becomes wearisome.)
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَسَىٰ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَداً﴾.
That is, we will adopt him.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The most perceptive of people are three: al-ʿAzīz when he said to his wife ﴿أَكْرِمِي مَثْوَاهُ عَسَىٰ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ﴾; the daughter of Shuʿayb when she said to her father ﴿إنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ القَوِيُّ الأَمِينُ﴾; and Abū Bakr when he appointed ʿUmar [as his successor]."

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾.
It is said: Al-ashudd is thirty-three years.
It is also said: thirty.
And most [say it is] from nineteen years to forty.
Rabīʿa, Zayd ibn Aslam and Mālik said: Al-ashudd is puberty.
Sībawayh holds that it is the plural of shidda, like niʿma and anʿum.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً﴾.
The difference between "the wise (al-ḥakīm)" and "the knowing (al-ʿālim)" is that the wise is the one who acts according to his knowledge and refrains from ugly things; and from this is said ḥakamat al-dābba (the bridle-ring of the riding animal).

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَاوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِ﴾.
The meaning of "So-and-so (masc.) rāwada So-and-so (fem.)" is that he solicited her for indecency; mention of the indecency is left out because the listener knows it.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, come here.
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: Do not be pedantic in the Qurʾān; it is only like one of you saying "halumma" and "taʿāla" (come). Then ʿAbd Allāh read ﴿وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ﴾ with fatḥa on the hāʾ and the tāʾ.
It is narrated from Mujāhid and ʿIkrima that they read ﴿وَقَالَتْ هِئْتُ لَكَ﴾ with the hamza.
Qatāda said: Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿هِئْتُ لَكَ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: That is, I have made myself ready for you.
Al-Kisāʾī rejected this reading and said: I do not know (هِئْتُ لَكَ) in the meaning of "I have made myself ready". But according to the Basrans it is good, because one says هاءَ الرجلُ يَهَاءُ and يهيءُ هَيْأَةً; so هَاءَ يَهِيءُ is like جَاءَ يَجِيءُ, and هِئْتُ is like جِئْتُ.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُ رَبِّيۤ﴾.
The meaning may be: Allah is my Lord, so I will not disobey Him.
And the meaning may be: The king is my lord (rabbī), i.e. my master.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ﴾.
That is, We make clear to you; and al-qāṣṣ is the one who presents the story (qiṣṣa) as it truly is.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾.
That is, by Our revealing.
Then He said: ﴿وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَافِلِينَ﴾.
That is: among those unaware of the story of Joseph, because he had not read any book before that; he only came to know it through revelation.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لأَبِيهِ يٰأَبتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾.
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said — and this is Qatāda's wording: The eleven stars are his brothers, and "the sun and the moon" are his father and his mother.
Maʿmar said: Someone other than Qatāda said: his father and his maternal aunt.
Someone else said: He interpreted "the eleven stars" as eleven men by whom light is sought as light is sought from the stars; he interpreted the moon as his father, and he interpreted the sun as his mother or his maternal aunt.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād said: The interpretation of Joseph's ﷺ dream came after forty years, and that is the furthest limit of a dream.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰبُنَيَّ لاَ تَقْصُصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَىٰ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيْداً﴾.
That is, lest they scheme against you.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ﴾.
That is, He chooses you. Its origin is from جَبَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ, i.e. I gathered the thing; and from it is جَبَيْتُ الماء في الحوض (I collected the water in the basin).
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلأَحَادِيثِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, the interpretation of dreams.
Someone else said: That is, the accounts of the nations.
Then He said, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ﴾.
So he informed him that he would be a prophet, because he said: ﴿كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَآ عَلَىٰ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّقَدْ كَانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آيَاتٌ لِّلسَّائِلِينَ﴾.
It is said: insight.
It is also said: That is, a lesson.
And it is narrated that in some of the codices it is "عبرةٌ للسائلين" (a lesson for those who ask).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالُواْ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾.
That is, a group.
One of the lexicographers said: Al-ʿuṣba is from ten to forty.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
That is, he has gone astray in his love of Joseph, not in his religion.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱقْتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضاً﴾.
There is an omission (ḥadhf) in it; the meaning is: or cast him into a land where he will be far from your father. This omission is indicated by ﴿يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ﴾, i.e. it will be free for you.
﴿وَتَكُونُواْ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾, i.e. you will be, after destroying him, ﴿قَوْماً صَالِحِينَ﴾, i.e. repentant.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلاۤ أَن رَّأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the people of ḥadīth and the early authorities hold is that he was inclined towards her (hamma bihā) until Jacob ﷺ was made to appear before him.
Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār narrated to us: Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ — he is Ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī — from Ibn Abī Mulayka, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked: "How far did Joseph's inclination go?" He said: "He sat down to undo a belt-purse of his, and he was called: O Joseph, do not be like the bird that commits fornication while it has its feathers and then is left sitting without feathers. But he did not take heed at the call; then he saw the proof of his Lord, so he fled and was terrified."
In the narration of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abī Mulayka, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās how far Joseph's inclination went, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: He sat between her legs, and he saw Jacob ﷺ.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Mujāhid, who said: He undid his trousers; then Jacob appeared before him and said to him: "O Joseph!", and he turned and fled.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Jacob was made to appear before him, and he struck his chest, and his desire went out through his fingertips.
Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, who said: He saw the image of Jacob saying to him: "Joseph, Joseph."
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: He saw the image of Jacob on the ceiling of the house saying: "O Joseph, O Joseph."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said something similar to this. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām said: One of those who speak about the Qurʾān by their own opinion has claimed that Joseph ﷺ was not inclined towards her. He holds that the speech ends at His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ﴾; he said: then He began anew and said ﴿وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلاۤ أَن رَّأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ﴾, meaning: had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have been inclined towards her. He argued from His saying ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بالغَيْبِ﴾ and from His saying ﴿وَاسْتَبَقَا البَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ﴾. But Ibn ʿAbbās and those below him do not disagree that he was inclined towards her, and they are more knowledgeable about Allah and the interpretation of His Book, and too reverent towards the prophets to speak about them without knowledge.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This statement of Abū ʿUbayd is good and clear for whoever has not inclined to caprice. And what he mentioned of their argument from His saying ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بالغَيْبِ﴾ is not binding, because he did not commit the sin.
Moreover, it is authentically established in the ḥadīth that Gabriel ﷺ said to him, when he said ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بِالغَيْبِ وَأنَّ اللهَ لاَ يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الخَائِنِينَ﴾: "Not even when you were inclined?" So he said: ﴿وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إن النَّفْسَ لأَمَّارةٌ بالسُّوءِ﴾.
Likewise their argument from His saying ﴿وَاسْتَبَقَا البَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ﴾ is not binding, because it is possible that this was after the inclinations.
Al-Ḥasan said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, did not mention the sins of the prophets to reproach them with them; rather He mentioned them so that you would not despair of repentance.
It is also said: The meaning of ﴿وَهَمَّ﴾ is that it is something that crosses the heart, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever intends (hamma) an evil deed and then does not do it, it is not written against him." So this is among what crosses the heart; and had he been inclined towards her intending to commit it, that would have been grave.
And in the ḥadīth: "I seek the forgiveness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, a hundred times in the day and the night."
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have made clear the view of those among the people of ḥadīth and narrations whose view is to be relied on.
And the meticulous lexicographers hold their view.
Abū Isḥāq said: It is far-fetched to say "I struck you, were it not for Zayd" and "I was inclined towards you, were it not for Zayd"; the [proper] speech is only "Were it not for Zayd, I would have been inclined towards you." So had it been "وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ" and "ولَهَمَّ بِهَا لولا أن رأى برهان ربه" (and he would have been inclined towards her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord), it would be permissible, though far-fetched. The meaning is only: had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have carried out what he was inclined to.
One of the lexicographers said: The meaning is: and he was intent on بدفها. [Translator's note: «بدفها» is as printed; it is most likely a misprint for «بدفعها», "on pushing her away".]
And His saying, exalted be His majesty: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوۤءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ﴾.
Al-sūʾ (evil) is betraying his master, and al-faḥshāʾ (indecency) is committing the indecent act.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Jannād narrated to us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Jarawī narrated to us: Abū Marwān narrated to me — and he praised him well — he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir narrated to me concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوۤءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ﴾. He said: Al-sūʾ is ugly reputation, and al-faḥshāʾ is fornication.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱسُتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means Joseph and the wife of al-ʿAzīz.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى ٱلْبَابِ﴾.
That is, they came upon him; and at that a scheme occurred to her, so she said: ﴿مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوۤءًا إِلاَّ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾.
Abū Hurayra said: Three spoke in the cradle: Joseph's [witness], Jesus ﷺ, and Jurayj's [witness].
Sharīk narrated from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: He was a child in the house — or he said: in the cradle; Sharīk was unsure.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: He was a child in the house.
Hilāl ibn Isāf said: Three spoke in the cradle; one of them was Joseph's [witness].
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He was a bearded man.
Sufyān said, from Jābir, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: He was one of the king's intimates.
ʿIkrima said: He was not a child; rather he was a wise man.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, who said: He was a man.
Abū ʿĀṣim narrated from al-Muthannā, from al-Qāsim: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾ — he said: his shirt.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾; he said: The tearing of the shirt is the witness.
And al-qadd in the language is cutting.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّهُ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ﴾.
The meaning: your saying ﴿مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءاً﴾ is part of the scheming of you women.
Then he said ﴿يُوسُفُ أعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا﴾, i.e. do not divulge it.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنبِكِ﴾.
And it is narrated that he had little jealousy.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ٱمْرَأَةُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ تُرَاوِدُ فَتَاهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبّاً﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿شَغَفَهَا﴾: it overpowered her.
ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It entered beneath her shaghāf.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to one thing, because al-shaghāf is the membrane of the heart; so the meaning is: love of him reached her shaghāf and overpowered her heart. The poet said:
وَقَدْ حَالَ هَمٌّ دُونَ ذَلِكَ دَاخِلٌ * دُخُولَ الشَّغَافِ تَبْتَغِيهِ الأَصَابِعُ
(A care has come in the way of that, entering as the heart's membrane is entered, the fingers seeking it out.)
It has also been said that al-shughāf is a disease; and al-Aṣmaʿī recited from the rajaz poet:
* "يَتْبَعُهَا وَهِيَ لَهُ شُغَافُ" *
(He follows her, and she is a heart-sickness to him.)
And it is narrated from Abū Rajāʾ and Qatāda that they read ﴿قَدْ شَعَفَهَا حُبّاً﴾ with the ʿayn, undotted and with fatḥa.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its meaning according to most lexicographers is: it has carried her off in every direction, because the shaʿafāt of mountains are their summits; and شُعِفَ بذلك شَعْفاً, with sukūn on the ʿayn, i.e. he became infatuated with it. Except that Abū ʿUbayd recited the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
أَيَقْتُلُنِي وَقَدْ شَعَفْتُ فُؤَادَهَا * كَمَا شَعَفَ المَهَنُؤةَ الرَّجُلُ الطَّالِي
(Would he kill me, when I have set her heart burning, as the tar-smearing man burns the tarred she-camel?)
He said: So the burning and the ardour of love were likened to that.
And it is narrated from al-Shaʿbī that he said: Al-shaghaf is love, and al-shaʿaf is madness.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ﴾.
It is asked: How could this be called scheming (makr)? The answer is: she had let them into her confidence and asked them to keep it secret, but they divulged her secret; so that was called scheming.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, who said: Al-muttakaʾ — with doubling — is food, and al-mutk — without doubling — is citron.
Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Al-muttakaʾ is food.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: Al-muttakaʾ is food.
It is also said: Al-muttakaʾ is anything one reclines on at food, drink or conversation. This is what is well known among the lexicographers, except that the narrations have been authentically transmitted with that [i.e. "food"].
Al-Qutabī reported that one says اتَّكأْنَا عند فلان, i.e. we ate [at So-and-so's].
It has been said that al-mutk is al-zumāward [a kind of meat-and-egg roll]. And it is said: one says بتكَهُ when he cuts it and splits it, so it is as though the mīm is a substitute for the bāʾ, as one says lāzim and lāzib, among many parallels to it.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُ أَكْبَرْنَهُ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: They held him to be great.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the correct [view]. Whoever said "they menstruated (ḥiḍna)" has brought something unknown; and "ḥiḍna" is not transitive.
And the meaning: he awed them, so they held him to be great.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: Notching with the knife.
Mujāhid means that it was not a cutting by which the hand is severed; it was only a scratch and a notch. It is well known that when a person scratches his companion's hand, it is said: "He has cut his hand."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْنَ حَاشَ للَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, Allah forbid (maʿādha Allāh).
What he said is good. Its origin is from your saying "So-and-so is in the ḥashā of So-and-so", i.e. on his side. So when you say "ḥāshā li-Zaydin", its meaning is: setting Zayd aside; and ﴿حَاشَ للهِ﴾, i.e. Allah has set this apart from this.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا بَشَراً إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
And it has been read "ما هذا بِشِرَىً" (this is not one to be bought), i.e. something purchased.
The first is more likely, because after it comes "إنْ هَذَا إلاَّ مَلَكَ كَرِيمٌ", and because something like بِشِرىً would be written in the codex with a yāʾ.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَاوَدتُّهُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ فَٱسَتَعْصَمَ﴾.
The meaning of «فاستعصم»: so he refused.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ﴾.
It is narrated that al-Zuhdī read ﴿قال ربِّ السِّجنُ أحبُّ إِليَّ﴾.
And its meaning is: that I be imprisoned is dearer to me.
And whoever reads with kasra, "السِّجْنُ", its meaning for him is: the place of imprisonment is dearer to me than what they call me to.
[Translator's note: the name is printed «الزهدي», probably for al-Zuhrī; and the reading attributed to him is printed with kasra, although the explanation "that I be imprisoned" implies the maṣdar al-sajn with fatḥa, as opposed to the kasra reading discussed next. Translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِلاَّ تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْجَاهِلِينَ﴾.
One says صَبَا إلى اللَّهْوِ صُبُوًّا (he inclined to amusement).
And al-Farrāʾ reported صَبَأ, when one inclines to it.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾.
So He construed it according to the meaning, because in his words there is the meaning of supplication, even though no supplication is mentioned.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ ٱلآيَاتِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the tearing of the shirt.
Qatāda said: He means the tearing of the shirt and the notching of the hands.
Then He made clear what occurred to them, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ﴾.
They may have been two young men, or they may have been two old men; the Arabs use this [word "fatā" for both].
Then He said, exalted be His mention: ﴿قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّيۤ أَرَانِيۤ أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً﴾.
There are several views on this, among them:
That khamr here means grapes; among them, that the meaning is "grapes of wine"; and among them, that it is like your saying "[I see myself] pressing oil", i.e. pressing what ends up as oil, as he said:
الحمد لله العليِّ المنَّان * صار الثريد في رؤوس العيدان
(Praise be to Allah, the Most High, the Bestower: the tharīd has come to be on the tops of the stalks.)
He means only the ears of grain, and he called them tharīd (sopped bread) because tharīd comes from them. This is a good view.
The first is the clearest of them, and the exegetes hold it.
Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd informed me: Wahb ibn Jarīr, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning His saying ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَرَانِيۤ أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً﴾: he said: Khamr is grapes; the people of ʿUmān call grapes khamr.
Then He said, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلآخَرُ إِنِّي أَرَانِيۤ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزاً تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them: We see that you are good at interpreting dreams.
The other view: It is narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he used to help the wronged, visit the sick, support the weak, and make room for men.
Then he turned aside from answering them to something other than what they had asked him about, and said "لا يأتيكما" (there will not come to you).
There are two views on this:
One of them: Ibn Jurayj said: He did not want to interpret the dream for them, so he turned aside from their question; but they did not leave him until he interpreted it.
Someone else said: He wanted to let them know that he was a prophet and that he knew it through the unseen, so he said: ﴿لاَ يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِ إلاَّ نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ يَأْتِيكُمَا﴾.
And it is narrated that when the king wanted to kill someone, he would send him a particular food which he never varied.
Then he let them know that this knowledge was from Allah, not by soothsaying or astrology, saying: ﴿ذَلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي﴾.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then he let them know that he was a believer, saying: ﴿إِنِّي تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لاَّ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ﴾.
Then he said afterwards: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى النَّاسِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللهِ عَلَيْنَا﴾: that He made us prophets; ﴿وَعَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: that we were sent to them as messengers.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t: Then after that he invited them to Islam, saying: ﴿يٰصَاحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَّفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَاحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰصَاحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْراً﴾.
That is, he will be in charge of the king's drink.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: When he interpreted the dream for them, they said: "We did not see anything." So he said: ﴿قُضِيَ الأمرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ﴾, i.e. it has come to pass as I said, whether it was true or false.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: With the king. And it is well known in the language that a master is called rabb. Al-Aʿshā said:
رَبِّي كَرِيمٌ لاَ يُكَدِّرُ نِعْمَةً * وَإذَا تُنوشِدَ بالمَهَارِقِ أنْشَدَا
(My lord is noble; he does not sully a favour, and when adjured by the written scrolls, he answers.)
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنْسَاهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Satan made Joseph forget the remembrance of his Lord — to ask Him and humble himself before Him — so that he said to one of the two young men: ﴿ٱذْكُرْنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾.
Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Were it not for Joseph's word — meaning his saying ﴿ٱذْكُرْنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾ — he would not have remained in prison as long as he remained."
He said: Then al-Ḥasan would weep and say: "When a matter befalls us, we complain to people."
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَبِثَ فِي ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: He means that he remained in prison seven years.
Wahb said: Job remained in affliction seven years, and Joseph remained in prison seven years.
Al-Farrāʾ said: They mentioned that he remained seven [years] after five years, after his saying ﴿ٱذْكُرْنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾. He said: And al-biḍʿ is what is less than ten.
Al-Akhfash said: Al-biḍʿ is from one to ten.
Qatāda said: Al-biḍʿ is between three, nine and ten; and this is the view of al-Aṣmaʿī.
Al-ʿUtbī said: Abū ʿUbayda said: Al-biḍʿ is not a full decade, nor half a decade; we hold that it is from one to four.
Quṭrub said: Al-biḍʿ is what is between three and nine.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said that the more correct of the two is the view of al-Aṣmaʿī, because Dāwūd ibn Hind narrated from al-Shaʿbī that the Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, when he made a wager with Quraysh about the Byzantines defeating the Persians, and six years passed — and Abū Bakr had said "They will be victorious within a few (biḍʿ) years" — the Prophet ﷺ said: "How much is biḍʿ?" He said: "What is between three and nine." So Abū Bakr wagered with them again and increased [the stake], and after that the news came that the Byzantines had defeated the Persians.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّيۤ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ﴾.
Al-ʿijāf are those that have reached the utmost degree of emaciation.
And the meaning of ʿabarta al-ruʾyā (you interpreted the dream) is: you brought it out of the state of sleep into the state of wakefulness; it is taken from al-ʿibr, which is the riverbank.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلأَحْلاَمِ بِعَالِمِينَ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: That is, mixtures. And al-ḍighth according to the lexicographers is likewise; anything mixed together — of herbs, grass or other things — is called ḍighth.
That is, this dream is jumbled and not clear.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Sufyān from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾: after a while.
ʿAffān narrated from Hammām, from Qatāda, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read "وادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أَمْهٍ"; but the well-known reading of Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima is ﴿وادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أَمَةٍ﴾.
They explained it as "after forgetting". The two meanings are close, because he remembered after a while and after forgetting.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿أَنَاْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾.
That is, I will inform you.
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿آتِيكُمْ بتأويله﴾ (I will bring you its interpretation), and said: How could the boor inform them?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of "I will inform you" is sound and good, i.e. I will inform you once I have asked.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَرْسِلُونِ. يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ﴾.
There is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech; the meaning is: so he went and said: O Joseph.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّعَلِّيۤ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
The meaning may be: so that they may know the interpretation of the king's dream.
And it may be: so that they may know of your situation, and you will come out of prison.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
﴿قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ دَأَباً﴾.
That is, in succession and as is your custom.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning of ﴿تُحْصِنِونَ﴾ is: you store away.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿يَعْصِرُون﴾: grapes and oil.
And it is read "تَعْصِرُونَ", "يَعْصِرُونَ" and "يُعْصَرُونَ".
Abū ʿUbayda claimed that the meaning of yaʿṣirūn is "they will be saved", from al-ʿuṣra and al-ʿaṣar, both meaning a place of refuge. And Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar recited [a verse] of Abū Zubayd:
صَادِياً يَسْتَغِيثُ غَيْرَ مُغَاثٍ * وَلَقَدْ كَانَ عَصْرُهُ المَنْجُودِ
(Thirsting, crying for help, unhelped — and he had been the refuge of the terrified.)
Al-manjūd is the terrified.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best [view] on this is that its meaning is what Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jurayj said about yaʿṣirūn.
As for "تُعْصَرُونَ", its meaning is "you will be rained upon", from His saying ﴿وأنْزَلْنَا مِنَ المُعْصِرَاتِ ماءً ثَجَّاجاً﴾.
And likewise the meaning of "تُعْصِرُون".

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ﴾.
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ marvelled at his patience and said: "Had I been in his place and then the messenger came, I would have hastened [out]."
Then he said: ﴿فَاسْأَلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱللاَّتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾.
He did not mention the wife of al-ʿAzīz among them, out of good companionship and courtesy on his part.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Pharaoh gathered the women and said to them: "Did you solicit Joseph?" The wife of al-ʿAzīz said: ﴿ٱلآنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَاْ رَاوَدْتُّهُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾. Joseph said: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بِالغَيْبِ إنَّ اللهَ لاَ يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الخَائِنِينَ﴾. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, said — and nudged him — "Not even when you were inclined?" So he said: ﴿وَمَا أُبَرِّئ نَفْسِي إنَّ النَّفْسَ لأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is obscure speech according to the Arabic grammarians, because Joseph's speech is mixed with what precedes it and not separated from it. Do you not see that He reported of the wife of al-ʿAzīz that she said ﴿أَنَاْ رَاوَدْتُّهُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾, and then Joseph's saying ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بالغَيْبِ﴾ was joined to it?
Its parallel is ﴿إنَّ الملوكَ إذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوا أعِزَّةَ أهْلِهَا أذِلَّةً وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is another interpretation of the verse.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Joseph said: "Go back to your lord and ask him: what about the women who cut their hands? My Lord is aware of their scheming. ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بِالغَيْبِ﴾."
Ibn Jurayj said: This is a case of placing before and after (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the Qurʾān.
He said: He wanted to make his excuse clear before he came out of prison. So, on this interpretation, Joseph said this in prison.
And on the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās, Joseph said it after he had come out of prison, when the king gathered him with the women.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both interpretations are good, and Allah knows best the truth of that.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: The meaning of ﴿حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ is: it has become clear.
Abū Isḥāq said: It is taken from al-ḥiṣṣa (share), i.e. the share of truth has become distinct from the share of falsehood.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي﴾.
That is, I will make him exclusively mine, with no one else sharing him with me.
Then He said, exalted be His mention: ﴿فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مِكِينٌ أَمِينٌ﴾.
That is, we have come to see clearly your trustworthiness and your innocence of what you were accused of. [Translator's note: the source prints «بد تَبَينَّا», evidently for «قد تبيَّنَّا».]
﴿قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِي عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, over its wealth.
﴿إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
That is, a guardian of the wealth, and I know the places in which it ought to be put. [Translator's note: the source prints «الماوضع», evidently for «المواضع» (places).]

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ٱئْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَّكُمْ مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ﴾.
It is said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: he asked them about their affairs, and when they informed him and the conversation led to this, he said: ﴿ٱئْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَّكُمْ مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلاَ تَرَوْنَ أَنِّيۤ أُوفِي ٱلْكَيْلَ وَأَنَاْ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنْزِلِينَ﴾.
It is said: [He said this] because he had treated them with excellent hospitality.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ﴾.
It is said: What is meant by al-fitya and al-fityān here is slaves.
Then he said: ﴿ٱجْعَلُواْ بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنْقَلَبُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two views on this:
One of them: that the meaning is: "When they see the goods in their saddlebags — and they are the price of the food — they will return, because they are prophets who do not take anything without a price."
It is also said: When they see the goods in the saddlebags, they will know that this could only come about by Joseph's doing, so they will return.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَلْ آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Because they had said about his brother: "أرسله معَنَا غَداً نَرْتَعْ وَنَلعب وإنَّا لهُ لحافظونَ" (Send him with us tomorrow to enjoy himself and play, and we will surely guard him).
So they had guaranteed to him that they would guard both of them.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي﴾.
The meaning may be: What more could we want, when our goods have been returned to us?
And the meaning may be: We do not seek anything [more], with "mā" being negating.
Then He said: ﴿وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا﴾.
One says مَارَ أهله، يَمِيرُهم، مَيْراً ومَيرَةً when someone brings his family their provisions from one land to another.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: Because he used to give each man of them a camel-load.
Mujāhid said: He means a donkey-load.
Some of them said: The donkey is called baʿīr — meaning that it is a dialect usage.
As for the lexicographers, they do not know of the donkey being called baʿīr; and Allah knows best what he meant.
Then He said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ﴾.
That is, easy for him.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ﴾.
That is, unless you perish and are overpowered.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ﴾.
That is, guarantor.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ يٰبَنِيَّ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ مِن بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَٱدْخُلُواْ مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He feared the evil eye for them.
Someone else said: The evil eye is real, because the Prophet ﷺ used to seek protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, saying: "I seek protection for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every evil eye (lāmma)."
It is also said: He disliked that something should befall them and that it then be imagined to be from the evil eye, so that one would incur sin in that.
The evidence for the soundness of this view is the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "When you hear of the plague in a land, do not go to it…"
Another answer: that he disliked their entering [together] so that they would be regarded with suspicion; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows best.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ حَاجَةً﴾.
It is said: The meaning is that had something been decreed against them, it would have befallen them, whether they entered together or separately.
It is also said: The meaning is: had it been decreed that the evil eye should strike them, it would have struck them separately just as it would strike them together.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِلاَّ حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means his fear of the evil eye for them.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ آوَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ﴾.
One says آويتُ فلاناً, with the long vowel (madd), when you draw someone close to you; and أَويتُ إليه, i.e. I took refuge with him.
And the meaning of ﴿فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ﴾ is: do not grieve; from al-buʾs (misery).

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: It is the king's drinking vessel.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the vessel from which the king drinks.
Shuʿba narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿صُوَاعُ المَلِكِ﴾: a thing of silver resembling the makkūk [a measuring vessel], of gold and silver, studded with jewels, placed on the head.
And al-ʿAbbās had one in the Jāhiliyya.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ﴾.
That is, he announced and called out. One says آذَنْتُ, i.e. I announced, and أَذَّنْتُ, i.e. I announced time after time.
And the meaning: O people of the caravan.
And [how could] he say ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ﴾ when they had not stolen the cup?
It is said: Because they had taken Joseph and sold him, so he considered it permissible to say to them: "You are thieves."
It is also said: It may be that the cup was placed in their saddlebags without the one who called out to them knowing of it, so he would be [saying something] untrue.
Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: That is, your condition is the condition of thieves; and so is the speech of the Arabs. It is as though the caller reckoned that the people had stolen it, not knowing what Joseph had done.
It is also said: It may be that the caller's announcement was by Joseph's command, and he considered it permissible with regard to them because they had committed a theft on some occasion — meaning that theft, not their stealing of the cup.
One of the interpreters said: That was a mistake on Joseph's part, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, punished him, when they said to him: ﴿إنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَاْ بِهِ زَعِيمٌ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, guarantor (kafīl).
Qatāda said: That is, surety (ḥamīl).
Al-Farrāʾ said: The zaʿīm of a people is their chief and their spokesman.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is close to the first, because their surety is their chief.
Abū Umāma narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "And the zaʿīm is liable" — abridged.
By al-zaʿīm he ﷺ means the guarantor.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is narrated that they would not impose themselves on anyone wrongfully, nor threaten anyone's crops, and that they put muzzles on the mouths of their camels so that they would not wreak havoc in people's crops.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ﴾.
It is narrated that they had returned the goods that had been put in their saddlebags; i.e. how can one who returned what he found be a thief?

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿قَالُواْ فَمَا جَزَآؤُهُ إِن كُنتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ﴾.
It is said: This is the stratagem which Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلْمَلِكِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, under the king's authority. That is because the king's law was that when a person stole something [he was fined its like; and the law of Jacob ﷺ was that when a person stole,] he was enslaved; so for this reason he referred the judgement back to them.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلْمَلِكِ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
That is, except by His will, Exalted is He.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ﴾.
And it is read ﴿دَرَجَاتِ مَنْ نَشَاءُ﴾ (the ranks of whom We will), meaning "whom We will, by ranks".
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
It is said: until knowledge ends with Allah, exalted be His majesty.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: This one is more knowledgeable than that one, and Allah is above every knower.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "We were with Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, and he related a narration, and a man was amazed at it and said: Glory be to Allah! ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: What an evil thing you have said! Allah is the All-Knowing, and He is above every knower."

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They mean Joseph.
And it is narrated that he had seen an image being worshipped, so he took it and threw it away; he did that only in disapproval of anything other than Allah being worshipped.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ﴾.
Then He made clear what he kept secret, by His saying: ﴿قَالَ أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً﴾.
That is, you are the ones who truly stole, when you sold your brother.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمْ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ﴾.
That is, Allah knows best whether his brother stole or not.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا ٱسْتَيْأَسُواْ مِنْهُ خَلَصُواْ نَجِيّاً﴾.
That is, they despaired [and] left their brother, and withdrew by themselves conferring privately about how they could return to Jacob without their brother with them.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَّوْثِقاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It is said: "Their eldest" is Judah.
Mujāhid said: It is Simeon (Shamʿūn), and he was not their eldest in age, because Reuben (Rūbīl) was older than him.
Mujāhid holds that the meaning is "their senior said" [in intellect, and their chief, not their eldest in age. And Qatāda said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ﴾:] it is Reuben; he held that he was their eldest in age. And Allah knows best the truth of that.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ ٱلأَرْضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْذَنَ لِيۤ أَبِيۤ﴾.
He means the land of Egypt, since everyone is on the earth.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿#١٦٤٩؛رْجِعُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُواْ يٰأَبَانَا إِنَّ ٱبْنَكَ سَرَقَ﴾. [Translator's note: the beginning of the quotation is corrupted in the source («#١٦٤٩؛رْجِعُوۤاْ»); the word is «ٱرْجِعُوۤاْ».]
And it is reported that it has been read ﴿سُرِّقَ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar narrated to me: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Shabīb narrated to me: Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Abī Surayj narrated to us — they both said: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Dāwūd — he is Ibn Abī Hind — from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās [was heard] reading it: ﴿يَا أبَانَا إنَّ ابنَكَ سُرِّقَ﴾.
And Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar narrated to me: Ibn Shādhān narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Surayj al-Baghdādī narrated to us: I heard al-Kisāʾī reading ﴿يَا أبَانَا إنَّ ابْنَكَ سُرِّقَ﴾, with ḍamma on the sīn.
And "سُرِّقَ" bears two meanings:
One of them: he was accused of theft.
The other: theft became known of him.
And the meaning of ﴿بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ﴾ is: rather, [your souls] have made [something] seem attractive.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَٰأَسَفَىٰ عَلَى يُوسُفَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, O my grief!
Mujāhid said: That is, O my distress!
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱبْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, he did not say anything ill.
And so it is in the language: one says "So-and-so is kaẓīm" and "kāẓim", i.e. grieving without complaining of his grief.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "تفتأ", i.e. you will not cease.
Mujāhid said: "تَفْتَؤُ", i.e. you will [not] slacken.
The first is what is known among the lexicographers; one says ما فَتِئَ and ما فَتَأ, i.e. he did not cease.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضاً﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujāhid: That is, short of death.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, worn out and wasted.
The two views are close. One says أحْرَضَهُ المَرَضُ فَحَرِضَ وَيَحْرَضُ (illness wasted him, so he wasted away) when his sickness persists and he is worn out.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Al-ḥāriḍ is one corrupted in body and mind, and likewise al-ḥaraḍ.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Al-ḥaraḍ is one whom grief has melted away.
Someone else said: From it is حَرَّضتُ فلاناً, i.e. I corrupted his heart.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْهَالِكِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, among the dead.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-bathth is the most intense grief.
Qatāda said: ﴿ولا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللهِ﴾, i.e. of His mercy.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, onto the throne-couch (al-sarīr).
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَخَرُّواْ لَهُ سُجَّدَاً﴾.
Qatāda said: This was part of their greeting.
Ibn Jurayj said: They used to do this as the Persians do.
And [another] meaning: and they fell down in prostration to Allah.
The first view is more likely; it is a prostration not of worship. Even though Muslims have been forbidden this, it was, according to what is narrated, a greeting they had.
Al-Ḥasan said: Between Joseph's parting from his father and his reunion with him there were eighty years, during which Jacob did not cease weeping for a single hour; and there was no one at that time more honoured before Allah than Jacob ﷺ.
He was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, he lived twenty-three years after meeting Jacob, and he died at the age of one hundred and twenty.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلأَحَادِيثِ﴾.
"Min" here may be partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), i.e. You have given me part of the kingdom and taught me part of the interpretation.
And it may be for specifying the genus (li-bayān al-jins), i.e. You have given me the kingdom and taught me the interpretation of events.
This answer is supported by ﴿تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, you are not able to guide whomever you wish.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن آيَةٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾.
That is: how many a sign there is in the raising of the heavens without pillars, in the courses of the sun, the moon and the stars, and in the earth — its palms and its crops! That is, they know them.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ وَهُمْ مُّشْرِكُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: It is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللهُ﴾.
Then when they are asked about His attributes, they describe Him with other than them, and ascribe a child to Him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿIkrima holds that "belief" here is their acknowledgement.

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿أَفَأَمِنُوۤاْ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَاشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾? [verse 107].
Mujāhid said: That is, [a punishment] that covers them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its meaning is: it envelops them; and from it is ﴿هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الغَاشِيَةِ﴾?
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
That is, suddenly, from where they do not reckon.

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هَـٰذِهِ سَبِيلِيۤ أَدْعُو إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ﴾.
That is, upon certainty; and from it is "So-and-so is mustabṣir (clear-sighted) about this."

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī narrated from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ﴾. She said: "The messengers despaired of the belief of those of their people who denied them, and they thought that those of their people who had believed had [come to] deny them, because of the affliction and trial that befell them."
Ibn Abī Mulayka narrated from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: Affliction and harm befell the believers, until the messengers thought that they had [come to] deny them because of what befell them.
Qatāda said: Until, when the messengers despaired of their people's belief, and were certain that their people had denied them, Our help came to them.
Qatāda holds that ẓann (thinking) here is certainty, and that is well known in the language. The meaning is that the messengers had been hoping that their people would believe; then they despaired of that, and the help came to them.
The first view is closer to the meaning, and it has a higher chain of transmission; and Allah knows best what He intended.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ﴾ without doubling and with ḍamma on the kāf.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two narrations from Ibn ʿAbbās about its meaning:
(a) Ibn Abī Mulayka narrated from him: that they weakened; he said: They were human beings.
(b) The second view: it is narrated from Sufyān, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "حتَّى إذا اسْتَيْأَسَ الرُّسُلُ" of their people's belief, and their people thought that they [the messengers] had been lied to, Our help came to them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The pronoun in "كُذِبُوا" refers back to the people on this view.
Mujāhid read ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ﴾ without doubling and with fatḥa on the kāf. [Translator's note: the quotation is printed with ḍamma on the kāf, although the text describes Mujāhid's reading as «كَذَبُوا» with fatḥa.]
And he explained it: and their people thought that they [themselves] had lied. In meaning it is like the one before it.
Two views are narrated from him concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ﴾:
One of them: until, when the messengers despaired of the punishment coming to their people.
And the second view is better, namely: until, when the messengers despaired of their people's belief.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means Joseph and his brothers.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَا كَانَ حَدِيثاً يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Sufyān said: He means the Torah, the Gospel and the [other] scriptures. ﴿وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَاعَةٍ مُّزْجَاةٍ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: That is, poor-quality silver coins that would not pass except at a discount.
Mujāhid said: That is, little.
Qatāda said: That is, scant.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: They had with them the wares of the Bedouins: clarified butter, wool and the like.
These views are close to one another. Its origin is from al-tazjiya, which is pushing and driving; one says "So-and-so yuzjī the camels", i.e. he drives them on. The meaning is that it is merchandise that is pushed along [with difficulty] and not accepted by everyone.
Mālik argued from His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَأَوْفِ لَنَا ٱلْكَيْلَ﴾ that the wage of the measurer and the weigher is due from the seller.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ لاَ تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّاحِمِينَ﴾.
Al-tathrīb is reproaching, blaming and spoiling a matter; and from it is ثَرَّبْتُ أمرَه, i.e. I spoiled his affair.
And from it is the ḥadīth: "When the slave-woman of one of you commits fornication, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and let him not yuthrib", i.e. let him not reproach her for the fornication.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلْعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ إِنِّي لأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "A wind arose, and he smelled the scent of the shirt from a distance of eight days' travel."
Then he said: ﴿لَوْلاَ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [were it not that] you would call me foolish.
ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, you would call me a liar.
The first view is the well-known one. One says فنَّده تفنيداً when someone declares another feeble-minded, as he said:
* "أَهْلَكَتْنِي باللَّوْمِ وَالتَّفْنِيدِ" *
(She has destroyed me with blame and accusations of dotage.)
And one says أفْنَدَ when someone speaks in error; al-fanad is error in speech and opinion, as the poet said:
إلاَّ سُلَيْمَانَ إذْ قَالَ المَلِيكُ لَهُ * قُمْ فِي البَرِيَّةِ فَاحْدُدْهَا عنِ الفَنَدِ
(Except Solomon, when the King said to him: Rise among creation and restrain it from folly.)

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱدْخُلُواْ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ آمِنِينَ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: That is, "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if Allah wills."
He said: This is a case of placing before and after (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the Qurʾān.
Ibn Jurayj holds that they had already entered Egypt, so how could he say ﴿ٱدْخُلُواْ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾?
